messages.subject: R² for Second-Order Construct
parts:
Hi everyone,

I'm trying to fit a reflective first-order, formative second-order model using lavaan. Let's say I use the following model, how can I obtain the unique proportion of variance in the second-order construct (speed; measured by three reflective indicators) that is explained by each first-order construct (visual and textual)?

# specify the model
HS.model <- '
    visual  =~ x1 + x2 + x3      
    textual =~ x4 + x5 + x6
    speed   =~ x7 + x8 + x9
    speed   ~ visual + textual'

# fit the model
fit <- cfa(HS.model, data=HolzingerSwineford1939)

# display summary output
summary(fit, rsquare=T, fit.measures=TRUE)
inspect(fit, "R2")


Using inspect and summary do not seem to return the R²-values that I'm interested in as I would like to have values for visual and textual:

> inspect(fit, "R2")
   x1    x2    x3    x4    x5    x6    x7    x8    x9 speed 
0.596 0.179 0.338 0.725 0.731 0.702 0.324 0.523 0.442 0.227 

Do I have a misunderstanding here or do I just lack the knowledge of the correct function in R?


Thank you very much!

messages.author: bfa43814f6ba1969
messages.subject: Re: R² for Second-Order Construct
parts:
Hi,

You are regressing speed on textual and visual, and that R2 of speed is from that regression. Visual and textual are exogenous variables, so they do not have R2 values. R2 is a measure of variance explained by a set of variables. But that you probably know already. If you want to get the amount of variance explained uniquely by visual and textual, you need to look into different effect size statistics. The choice of effect size statistic depends on what exactly you want to quantify. See this article for an introduction

Kelley, K., & Preacher, K. J. (2012). On effect size. Psychological Methods, 17(2), 137.

As a side note, you should probably use the sem function instead of the cfa function when fitting models with latent regressions.

Mikko
